output.summary: A genus of long-lived, rosette-forming succulent plants native mainly to mountainous, arid Mexico, with some species also native to the southwestern United States. Numerous evergreen leaves persist after dying, often forming a skirt around the trunk. Historically, the crowns were baked or roasted and made into flour, while flowering stems were eaten raw, boiled or roasted.
output.edibilityNote: Historically, crowns were baked or roasted, dried and pounded into flour for cakes; flowering stems were eaten raw, boiled or roasted.
